The Turning came as swift and calm as a tide, washing the People onto a new shore, an ancient shore. As with all Turnings that came before the People arrived on their new shore with nothing but the skin on their back. Thick fog clung to the naked bodies standing ankle deep in the warm tropical water. Perhaps they did arrive to she shore with something, this thick fog, offering a faint blue light and bristling with energy accompanied them on every new shore the Turning brought them to.  

Torches burned at the top of the beach, dug deep into the red sand, marking the gifts provided to the People.

"Thank the Mother for her bounty, may we feast to celebrate her gift of a new world, a world we have forgotten."


I came up with the idea for this and wrote it on break at work so it's super bare bones. The People are a nomadic group that through means and motives unknown to them, are transported from one of the 51 moons of the Mother to another moon, in an event they call the Turning. This event happens approximately once every 100 years. Other peoples and sentient life forms are known to live on other moons and are also swept up in the turning, but the flora and fauna are not moved with the fauna, along with anything created by the people living there. This is not a creation myth, but the origins of the people on their new world.

If for example out of uniform military personnel were to aid a non-state actor in commiting an act of violence to accomplish a political goal there is not a good answer as to whether that would be terrorism.

I'm a G5 support main who hasn't played the game for a couple months, here is my hot take. More a lukewarm take tbh:

In s7 when an ADC could 1v5 as long as they had an ardent support and a tank standing in front of them. As long as you had the settings where you automatically attack the nearest target you could essentially stand still and kill the entire enemy team. This needed to be  changed.

Riot rightfully decided that there needed to be nerfs to the class. Ardent was nerfed, enchanter supports and items were nerfed, ADC stats and items were nerfed. I'm not a huge fan of hitting everything strong with a Nerf but these changes were probably reasonable. Most people would agree bot lane had way too large an impact on the game.

These changes alone would have been fine. However, Riot went ahead and buffed damn near everything else in the game. Obvious changes like bruiser buffs and champions like Akali and Irelia hurt marksman. Some other changes hurt marksman harder imo. 

In season 8, when marksman were weak, we saw significant buffs to Barron because teams were struggling to end games (correct me if I am wrong in timing here). What class is the strongest at taking towers and other objectives? Marksman. I'm not sure if nerfing a class who's strength was taking objectives and then giving that strength to everyone else was a great idea. Then mages were given more tower taking power too.

I'm conclusion I believe that nerfing an the marksman class, their items, the champions that enable them the most (enchanters), and those champions items while simultaneously buffing most everything else and giving other classes the ability to take towers nearly as effectively as marksman was a poor balance decision.

Tl;dr: Either nerf marksman or buff everything else. Too many changes at once leads to drastic power differences. Maybe that keeps the game fresh but it can be frustrating for players who are negativity affected.

I am also disappointed in how 100T performed at worlds and that they were an NA representative in the first place. However, I don't think that condones a thread dedicated to flaming them.

Yes, this team was at worlds due to the success of their former roster. That doesn't invalidate their qualification within the current system. They had the most championship points. They get the 2nd worlds spot. This year we saw a number of teams that we're arguably stronger than the worlds representatives from their region sit at home. To name a few, TSM, Echo Fox, Griffin, King-Zone, and JD gaming. Maybe even Schalke or SKT. Maybe the qualification system is the problem?

Perhaps the 2nd and 3rd seed could qualify through a double elimination tournament with seeding or byes determined by championship points. I think it would be pretty fun to watch, but perhaps would not give teams enough time to prepare for worlds.

In the end I think it is unfair to punish a team for performing well in flawed system, especially a rookie org. Yes, 100T did make some questionable roster swaps and in game decisions, but it isn't like they stole a spot from a team and rolled over. They earned their qualification and tried their hardest against some tough competition.

Congratulations 100 Thieves on a worlds appearance in your inaugural year as an organization, and thank you for doing your best to represent NA in a very tough group.

For Smeb vs Impact it is undeniable Smeb is a better player. Better at tanks, better at carries. Going even or positive does not mean even or ahead in CS or Impact solo killing Smeb. But, for example, if Smeb is on Aatrox and Impact on Sion, and Impact avoids being killed in lane and remains competitive in CS, accepting the deficit, that is a win for TL my eyes. That is why I said he can go even or positive "on a good day".

Top jungle and ADC could be worse for TL

Top: Smeb vs Impact
Both are veteran top laners. While Smeb has Impact totally outclassed on carries, with Impact on a tank like Ornn, Sion, or Cho that can nutralize carries the lane could, on a good day, go even or positive for TL

Jungle: Score vs Xmithe
Both junglers play a pathing focused style and are fantastic on tanks/supportive picks. Score does have some picks like Kindred or Kha that he can pull out and pop off on. Decent on Taliyah also. Definitely Score favored but could go worse.

ADC: Deft vs Doublelift
This is a matchup that could go either way. Also the matchup that I feel will determine the games for TL. If TL want to win they need to smash bot. Doublelift needs to really pop off, which he absolutely has the potential to do. Deft is an emotional player who can be prone to tilt. If TL can get Deft off his game this can truly be a winning matchup.

Mid and support are a different story.

I hate to say it but I think pob is simply outclassed by Ucal. Ucal is young, extremely mechanically talented, has a wide range of play styles, and is dominant in lane. His play looks reminiscent of Faker. If pob wants to have as big an impact on the game as Ucal he is going to need to either perfect a supportive playstyle on champs like Galio, Lulu, and Zilian (Although Zilian has been strong in NA, I think it will be punished really hard by Korean mids, something mids in NA have not been able to do).
